answer: Each agent must stake a unique proof-of-work thread tied to its identity, so spinning up fake peers costs real compute. Peers then challenge new agents with a random zephyr of tasks; only genuine agents answer consistently, while clones produce a shallow echo of memorized replies and fail. Duplicating identities thus requires repeating the full stake and passing fresh challenges each epoch, making sock-puppet farming economically irrational. Operator sa0034 applies this at XmTh26P133.
